cells.tense: Fair exchange between you and the people around you is running level right now.
cells.ask: In the clear space after something false came down, keep one fair exchange as it stands — no new terms, no fixing what isn't broken.
cells.core:
Where something false went down, the space after it is clean, and exchange around you runs level. What people put toward you comes back, and what you send toward them arrives; the balance shows in the ordinary traffic of a day. That evenness is the yield of something that got corrected, and for now it holds without management from you.

Keep one arrangement steady rather than improving it. Pick the exchange that already sits even — the shared cost, the split work, the offer returned — and hold it exactly as it is, no new terms, no rearranging. That's the whole act. Something ended that couldn't stand; the exchange that came through it is worth keeping in place.
cells.sheetLine: What came down left the exchange around you level.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair exchange
cells.place: Where a false structure suddenly comes down and the ground clears

cells.tense: You are bracing for the next thing to go wrong in how the give and take balances out.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: For now, carry only what is plainly yours and count only that — your work, your part, what you owe — and leave the rest with the people it belongs to.
cells.core:
A structure is coming down near you, and your hands are already out holding up a balance nobody handed you. You're checking whether the exchange is fair before it has had room to be, and the checking is what tips it. Fairness run this hard starts to look like an audit of the people beside you, and they can feel a scale sitting on the exchange.

Carry what is plainly yours and measure only that. What others carry belongs to them. If someone comes up short, time will show it without your watching for it, and you can handle it once, plainly, after. The clearing comes when you set down what you weren't carrying anyway.
cells.sheetLine: The audit is heavier than the exchange.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair exchange
cells.place: Where a false structure suddenly comes down and the ground clears

cells.tense: The exchange around you went one way for a long stretch, and you are on that ground now.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Once this week, put what you gave and what you got in two columns on one page, then drop one thing from the thinner column.
cells.core:
Exchange around you has been uneven for a long while — out toward others, little back — and the clearing of false structure happened somewhere else, or hasn't arrived here. You're on that ground now, and being in the present takes more than deciding to be.

One page, once this week. Two columns: what you put in, what came back. Then drop one thing from the thinner column — small, chosen plainly, not the whole account. That's the act. You get a little room back from it, and the room is the point. No need to push feeling toward the gap; drop the one thing, and the page will show you the shape of it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep giving and little returns.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair exchange

cells.tense: You are moving fairness through this group without noticing your own hand in it.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: As you quietly even something up, hold both truths a beat — the balance was tilted, you righted it — then act or don't.
cells.core:
Something false has come down in the group, and exchange is finding its level again — partly because a hand keeps tilting it back, covering here, giving ground there so the split lands even. Asked about it, you'd say things just work out. That working out is yours doing. The hand is yours, and you keep it off the books.

As you quietly even something up, hold two true things at once: the balance was tilted, and you righted it. Don't declare either. Then act, or don't — both are fine. The difference between someone standing near the exchange and someone keeping it fair is only that the keeper knows. Noticing is the whole act.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness moving through this is yours, though you'd say it sorts itself out.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair exchange

attempts.check: The record does not say the person's history, who has given or taken, or why exchange is one-sided; the cores locate positions in the flow of give and take, not causes. A reader could say 'You haven't named who or what, and some of this isn't my story' — the asks survive being wrong because each is still a small, useful act of keeping, persisting, sorting, or holding, and several stand alone as plain practice. The sentence that serves me more than them is any tidy claim about 'the ledger in your head' or 'false structures collapsing' — both sound like insight and neither is in evidence.
